nodes.label: Patient woke up with new-onset slurred speech, followed by worsening dysarthria and inability to swallow solid food without aspirating; no fever, headache, nausea, vomiting, dyspnea, facial droop, numbness, or tongue pain/swelling

Past medical history includes spine and lung conditions treated with decompression surgery and palliative radiation 4 months prior; two weeks before presentation, the patient enrolled in a phase I clinical trial

Physical examination showed hemodynamically stable vital signs, midline uvula, appropriate palate elevation and tongue protrusion, complete paralysis of the tongue, no tongue swelling/exudates/erythema/pharyngeal obstruction, intact remainder of cranial nerves, and normal strength and sensation in all extremities
MRI reveals enhancing nodules near the hypoglossal canals bilaterally with left skull base extension into paraspinal muscles
MRI shows no acute medullary infarct or local tongue/oropharyngeal lesion
Leptomeningeal metastasis involving the hypoglossal nerves
PET-CT results are unavailable for systemic staging
Tissue biopsy of the hypoglossal region has not been obtained
Leptomeningeal metastasis involving the hypoglossal nerves
Direct skull base metastasis invading the hypoglossal canals
Perineural spread of malignancy along the hypoglossal nerves
Neoplastic meningitis with cranial nerve involvement
Radiologist and pathologist independently interpret the bilateral enhancing hypoglossal canal nodules with skull base and paraspinal extension as strongly supporting neoplastic leptomeningeal seeding
